catalog.digestRule: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (spec §14.3) of this document with catalog.digest set to null; filled in at publication and stored with every reply and program that names this catalog

vocabulary.rule: tone is semantic color and nothing else; appearance is visual style and nothing else; kind picks a chart type; size picks a text size. No prop is named variant, color or style, and no component has an alias.

retired.variant: tone for color, appearance for style
retired.Heading: a Markdown heading
retired.rules: min, max, step or maxLength on the input itself
retired.name: value={$state}

vocabulary.retiredUse: checker hints only (E_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT, E_UNKNOWN_PROP); never taught, never accepted

capabilities.refs: The runner records $$tc(N) at store time (llm-runner output_refs). Without it every reference is unresolved, so inputs typed snapshot are not taught.
capabilities.handles: The runner (replies) or the show_ui provider (programs) records Artifact/File handles at store time. Without it inputs typed handle are not taught.
capabilities.network: The store-time network value: yes, no or unknown; missing reads unknown. It is part of every measurement key.
capabilities.maps: A computer-side maker produces the Map record at store time: a static raster and each place's position in it. No runner or provider has it in v1, so Map always draws unavailable and is never taught until a provider produces the record.

types.string: text; a number is not converted (E_PROP_TYPE)
types.number: exact decimal (spec §4.2); int: true requires an integer
types.boolean: true or false; a bare prop name means true
types.enum: one of the listed string literals
types.aspect: enum of the keys of vocabulary.aspect
types.gap: enum of the keys of vocabulary.gap
types.list<T>: a list whose elements have type T; items [a, b] bounds its length
types.rows: a list of records, written or computed
types.node<C>: one component of the named kinds
types.action: an action value (spec §7); only v1 steps

handle<K>.means: Artifact("id") or File("path") with a literal argument

types.address: an absolute http or https URL (spec §3.11); opened only on a tap, never fetched

paged.means: the name of a PagedList site

watch.means: the name of a Watch site

types.a|b: a union of the listed types; the value must have one of them
types.query: not a prop type: a program reads q.value, q.status, q.error and q.stale (spec §8.3) and passes plain values, which are part of the committed tree; no component renders a Query envelope itself

textStyles.headline: UIFont.TextStyle.headline
textStyles.metrics: L(style) is the line height of the style at the person's content size category, read from the platform once per measurement key; desktop maps the same names to its own fonts; a terminal layout maps every style to one row

geometry.rule: A component's height is a pure function of W, the text metrics, the stored network value, its own prop and child values in the committed tree, and, for a Citation, its index. It never reads a late input: snapshot contents, handle records, media bytes, map rasters or the envelope of a site the component renders itself. hIn lists everything the height reads; a prop whose type is late never appears in hIn.

inputs.W: width offered by the parent, in layout units
inputs.props:p: the value of prop p in the committed tree
inputs.tree:p: the text of prop p in the committed tree, measured by T or TW
inputs.count:p: the length of the list literal written for prop p
inputs.children: the measured heights of the children in the same revision
inputs.index: the citation's 1-based position among distinct sources in its reply or tree
inputs.placement: row (drawn in a transcript row) or page (a tool page or an opened show_ui page); fixed before measurement

geometry.grammar: h := number | k.name | k.gap.name | W | CW | L(style) | T(x, style, width, maxLines) | TW(x, style) | has(p) | n(p) | ar(p) | lines(x) | H(child) | p | h op h | min(h, h) | max(h, h) | ceil(h) | sum(...) | (h); op is + - * /; maxLines may be inf

functions.T: height of the sanitized text x in style s wrapped at width w, at most n lines with a trailing ellipsis; 0 when x is absent
functions.TW: width of x on one line in style s
functions.has: 1 when prop p is given (not absent), else 0
functions.n: length of the list literal of prop p
functions.ar: height/width ratio of the aspect value of p (vocabulary.aspect)
functions.H: the measured height of a child in the same revision

geometry.rounding: Each block component's height is rounded up to a whole layout unit before its parent adds it, so measured and drawn sums agree exactly; inline components round their box the same way before the paragraph measures them
geometry.clip: Every state of a component draws inside its measured box and clips; nothing draws outside the box or changes it
geometry.revision: A committed revision's heights never change. A reply's tags never change height after the final parse. On a page (a tool page or an opened show_ui page) a program takes the measured height of each new evaluate-measure-commit revision (spec §8.2). In the transcript a show_ui row never changes height after insertion: see rowFrame

rowFrame.rule: A show_ui row in the transcript keeps the height of its first committed revision, capped, plus an app-owned Open bar. Every later revision, the first-answer LoadingRoot included, draws inside that frame, top-aligned and clipped. Open shows the same instance on its page, where each revision takes its own measured height. Reason: a site answer arriving while the reader is elsewhere in the chat must never move the rows above them.
rowFrame.first: the load evaluation with every site at its default and the stored snapshot, the tree the checker's trial evaluation produced (spec §5.7); it needs no site answer, so a row from an old chat is measured before insertion without waiting
rowFrame.clipped: when a revision is taller than the frame, the Open bar says 'Open to see all'; otherwise 'Open'
rowFrame.toolRows: tool_row revisions (running to finished) are measured per revision as spec §2.3 says; whether they should freeze too is an open question

geometry.evaluator: The shared crate evaluates every geometry formula, for every app. Each platform supplies only the text-metric callbacks L, T and TW, implemented with the text system its views draw with and safe off the main thread. The terminal app's layout table in cells is left to the terminal app's maintainer.

states.loading: the input is not resolved yet (snapshot fetch, store-time record, decode); placeholder shapes inside the box
states.held: the snapshot is held (spec §4.8): pending look and the words 'Waiting for the tool'; it never fills in
states.unavailable: no record, unresolved, too_large, revoked, expired scope, evicted from the cache or an unsupported media type; an icon and 'Unavailable' inside the box
states.error: a failed Parse, an error value in a data prop, data of the wrong shape or a render cap exceeded; 'Couldn't show this' and the code inside the box
states.over: the reply, chat or app account (spec §9.1) has no room; 'Not shown' inside the box; drawn again when the account frees, through a new measured revision of the same height
states.text: the plain-text form (spec §11.3) used for copy, previews and notifications, and drawn clipped inside the box when the renderer cannot draw the component at all
states.sameBox: Every state above draws in the box geo.h gives; none has a height of its own
states.propError: An error value or a missing required prop (spec §5.6): when the prop is not in hIn the component draws its own error state in its normal box; otherwise it draws host.ErrorCell. Catalog failures known at the final parse of a reply are not states: the tag is literal text (spec §2.1)

accounts.spec: language spec §9.1 and §9.2; every number here repeats the spec and changes only with it

raster.decodeTo: the frame's pixel size; decode cost charged before allocation; decompression bombs refused from the header

accounts.visitRule: 1 per component node and 1 per text run laid out, plus each component's work.visits; reserved before layout against perRevision.visits
accounts.decodeRule: work.decoded is reserved against perRevision.decodedBytes and the retained accounts before decoding
accounts.overflow: a component whose reservation fails draws its over state; a reply keeps every other tag; a program whose tree needs more than perRevision aborts (spec §9.6)

rules.text: Display tags: write Markdown and add a tag where a visual helps. Tags draw in the apps.
Form: <Name prop="text" prop={value} /> or <Name …>content</Name>. A tag alone on its line is a block; inside a sentence it is inline. Never leave a blank line inside a tag.
A {value} may only be a number, "string", true, false, null, or a list [ … ] or record {key: …} of those.
It may also be $$tc(N), the output of tool call N, or Parse($$tc(N), "json" or "csv", {columns: {name: "number", other: "text"}}) to read it as rows. Declare number columns or charts can't plot them.
Pictures and files come by handle: Artifact("id") or File("relative/path").
Pictures and charts take data only by $$tc(N) or a handle, never by an address.
Replies have no state, variables, {expressions} in text, buttons or inputs; use show_ui for those.
tone is the color: neutral, info, success, warning or danger.
A tag that breaks a rule shows as its plain text and is reported to you on your next turn.
Each tag's size is fixed before data arrives: choose aspect and displayRows up front; more rows open on their own page.

reply.perComponent: signature line, then sum, then the examples whose needs the runner meets
reply.signature: <Name req: type, opt?: type = default>children</Name>; an enum of a shared vocabulary prints its name (tone, aspect); props allowed only in other profiles are omitted
reply.filter: Teach a reply component only if it is in the reply profile, the runner meets the component's own needs (Map needs maps) and at least one of its forms can be written with the runner's capabilities; drop props whose every allowed type needs a missing capability or is a tag (node<…>), since tags are not reply values; drop examples whose needs are not met. When the store-time network is known to be no, omit LinkCard and add: 'Links show as plain text in this session.'
reply.estimate: about 1,100 tokens with refs and handles (Map withheld: no v1 runner has maps) and about 560 without (3,350 and 1,950 characters; heuristic counts, no tokenizer was available; method in the companion)

from: the language's machine-readable rules: the language crate will export its function table and profile rules as JSON generated from the crate itself; the shape is left to the crate
this catalog filtered to the show_ui profile
the approved operation schemas for the calling session
show_ui.rule: Same signature format; every example compiled against the exact dialect, catalog digest and registry before it is published; operations the session cannot use are not taught

teaching.toolTemplates: Provider authors read this catalog and the tool_row/tool_page profiles directly; nothing is generated into model prompts for them

Badge.sum: A short status label inside a sentence, heading or table cell.

geo.note: label is text or the children's text on one line, cut with an ellipsis after clip.badge scalars or at W

ex.src: Tests finished. <Badge tone="success">17 passed</Badge> <Badge tone="danger">1 failed</Badge>

Styled.sum: Colored inline text; muted by default.

geo.h: part of the surrounding paragraph's text layout
geo.note: color does not change metrics, so the paragraph measures the same with or without the tag

ex.src: <Styled>Sizes come from a scan two minutes ago.</Styled>

Callout.sum: A highlighted note with an optional title.

geo.h: 2*k.calloutPad + has(title)*(T(title, headline, CW, 3) + k.gap.s) + T(body, body, CW, inf)
geo.note: body is description, or the children measured by the prose measurer at CW; both come from the bounded source or the committed tree

ex.src:
<Callout tone="warning" title="testPaging failed">
The second page came back empty. The fix is in `PageLoader.swift`.
</Callout>

Table.sum: Rows in a fixed viewport of displayRows rows; the person opens the rest.

columns.d: each entry is a record key, or {key, label} to show a different header

forms.note: the only form in replies; columns lists the record keys to show, in order, each as a key string or {key, label}; absent means the first row's keys, at most 8
program only: Col is a tag and tags are not reply values (spec §3.5)

data.shape: a list of records; a snapshot needs a format hint (Parse or show_ui data_format) and a list root

data.cells: string as written; number by FormatNumber (grouped, canonical decimals) and right-aligned; boolean true or false; null or missing empty; list or record …; an error value shows its code
data.more: when given, the open page drives LoadMore and auto_load_more for that PagedList (spec §8.6); the row itself never loads

geo.widths: each column gets max(k.colMin, TW(header, subheadline) + 2*k.cellPadH), where header is the entry's label or else its key; then the columns share what is left of W equally; wider than W scrolls sideways; cell text never widens a column
geo.note: one header row, exactly rows single-line rows, one footer; cells cut with an ellipsis, never wrap; a transcript row shows at most 10 rows, a page up to 50

states.loading: header (when column entries are literal), placeholder rows, footer 'Loading…'
states.ready: the first rows rows; footer 'N rows · Open' when there are more, else 'N rows'
states.empty: 'No rows' in the first slot; the other slots stay empty
states.error: header kept; message in the row slots; footer shows the code

Table.openPage: an app-owned page with every row (within the data caps), its own bounded lazy layout and measurement; it is never part of the row's height

work.caps: accounts.perRevision; cells beyond the viewport are not laid out

ex.src: <Table data={[{service: "api", state: "up"}, {service: "db", state: "down"}]} columns={["service", "state"]} />
<Table data={Parse($$tc(22), "json", {columns: {path: "text", bytes: "number"}})} columns={["path", {key: "bytes", label: "Size in bytes"}]} displayRows={6} />

Col.sum: One Table column: its label and its values.

geo.note: drawn by its Table; the row count is the longest column's length

LinkCard.sum: A card for a web page; a tap shows the full address before anything opens.

h.yes|unknown: 2*k.cardPad + T(title, headline, CW, 2) + has(description)*(k.gap.xs + T(description, subheadline, CW, 2)) + k.gap.xs + L(caption1)

geo.note: the last line is the canonical host in punycode; nothing is fetched to draw the card

LinkCard.net: yes or unknown: a card whose tap opens the address sheet (spec §3.11); no: its text form as a paragraph, with no activation

ex.src: <LinkCard href="https://limankahvesi.example/menu" title="Liman Kahvesi menu" />

Citation.sum: A numbered source marker after a sentence; a tap shows the source.

source.shape: any snapshot state, or a handle record; opened in the app's viewer through the broker (spec §7.5)

geo.note: index counts distinct sources in order of first appearance, so two citations of one source share a number

states.unavailable: the same chip, dimmed; the tap explains

ex.src: It opens at 7.<Citation source={$$tc(12)} />

Image.sum: One picture in a fixed frame.

image.shape: a handle record or a media snapshot whose MIME type is in accounts.raster.formats; resolved and flattened on the computer

geo.note: the picture fits inside the frame, letterboxed; the frame never follows the picture's size

ex.src: <Image image={Artifact("art_7f3a")} aspect="16:9" alt="The new login screen" />

ImageGroup.sum: Up to four pictures in a grid of fixed frames.

images.shape: as Image, per element; each slot resolves independently

geo.note: lit: the list must be written as a list literal, so the slot count is known from the source; a third picture leaves the fourth slot empty

ex.src: <ImageGroup images={[Artifact("art_k1"), Artifact("art_k2")]} aspect="4:3" caption="Inside and out" />

Map.sum: A static map of places from a tool output; no live tiles, no location.

places.shape: Parse of a JSON list of {name: string, lat: number, lon: number, note?: string}, plus the map record a computer-side maker prepares at store time: a static raster (accounts.raster) and each place's position in it
places.noRecord: unavailable; never a live tile or geocoding request from the phone

Map.v1: No runner or provider produces the map record in v1 (capabilities.maps), so every Map draws unavailable at its fixed size and no teaching names it. The tag stays valid so stored replies keep their geometry once a provider exists.
Map.draw: the raster with numbered pins at the recorded positions; a tap opens an app-owned list of the places as text

ex.src: <Map places={Parse($$tc(14), "json")} aspect="16:9" />

Chart.sum: A line or bar chart in a fixed frame.

data.d: in a reply only a reference: a chart's numbers come from a tool, never retyped

forms.note: x names the label column; y names one number column or a list of up to 8

data.shape: a list of records; x values are labels (text conversion); y values must be numbers, absent values leave gaps

data.wrongShape: a y value that is not a number or absent (E_TYPE), Series lengths that differ from labels (E_ARG), or more points or series than the caps (E_RENDER_LIMIT): the error state, never a partial chart

geo.note: axes, axis labels and a one-line legend draw inside the frame

ex.src: <Chart kind="bar" data={Parse($$tc(7), "csv", {columns: {seconds: "number"}})} x="suite" y="seconds" />

Series.sum: One named series of numbers for a Chart.

Card.sum: A container that stacks its content in a column or a row.

geo.widths: In a row, fixed children (inline components, Button, Buttons, InlineCode, Toggle) take min(their own width, the line); flexible children (Markdown blocks, TextContent, Card, Stat, Progress, LiveOutput, Table, Chart and the rest) share what is left equally, each at least k.flexMin. With wrap, children fill lines greedily in order; a flexible child ends its line. Without wrap, overflowing fixed children are cut from the end.
geo.note: align and justify move children inside the box; they never change its height

states.text: the children's text forms, one per line

CardHeader.sum: A title and optional subtitle at the top of a view.

geo.h: T(title, title3, W, 2) + has(subtitle)*(k.gap.xs + T(subtitle, subheadline, W, 2))

TextContent.sum: A block of plain text (not parsed as Markdown).

geo.style: small: footnote, default: body, large: title3

InlineCode.sum: A short piece of code or a command on one line.
InlineCode.note: Replies use Markdown code spans instead

CodeBlock.sum: Code in a box that scrolls sideways; at most maxLines lines show.

geo.h: 2*k.codePad + has(language)*(L(caption1) + k.gap.xs) + min(lines(codeString), maxLines)*L(mono) + (lines(codeString) > maxLines ? k.gap.xs + L(footnote) : 0)
geo.note: no wrapping, so W never changes the height; the last line says how many more lines the open page shows

FormControl.sum: A label, one input and an optional hint.

geo.h: T(label, subheadline, W, 2) + k.gap.xs + H(input) + has(hint)*(k.gap.xs + T(hint, footnote, W, 2))

Input.sum: A text or number field bound to a state of the same type.
Input.input: writes only values of the state's type; an emptied number field writes null (spec §4.10); text longer than maxLength is refused at the keyboard; a number outside min..max is kept but drawn with the warning tone

geo.note: a number field has lines 1

ex.src:
export let $doors = 1

<Input type="number" min={0} step={1} value={$doors} />

Select.sum: A menu of choices bound to a string state (a list state when multiple).
Select.input: writes the chosen item's value; with multiple, the list of chosen values in item order

geo.note: the menu opens in an app-owned popover outside the row

ex.src:
export let $region = "North"

<Select value={$region} items={[<SelectItem value="North" label="North" />, <SelectItem value="South" label="South" />]} />

Slider.sum: A slider bound to a number state.
Slider.input: writes min + step*k for the nearest whole k, clamped to max; a drag is coalesced to its latest value per frame (spec §8.2)
Slider.propRules: min < max and step > 0, else the error state (E_ARG) in the same box

ex.src:
export let $width = 4

<Slider min={2} max={10} step={0.1} value={$width} />

Toggle.sum: An on/off switch with a label, bound to a boolean state.

geo.h: max(k.tap, T(label, body, W - k.switchW - k.gap.m, 2) + 2*k.fieldPadV)

ex.src:
export let $failedOnly = false

<Toggle label="Failed runs only" value={$failedOnly} />

Button.sum: A button that runs its action on a tap; it never sends anything by itself.

act.busy: from activation until local steps and host handoffs finish (spec §7.3)

ex.src:
export let $page = 1

<Button label="Next" appearance="secondary" action={Set($page, $page + 1)} />

Buttons.sum: A row or column of Buttons.

geo.lines: greedy wrap of the buttons' widths at W with k.gap.s between

states.text: the buttons' text forms on one line

Tabs.sum: Tabs that show one TabItem at a time; the height is the tallest tab's.
Tabs.input: a tap selects a tab; when value is bound it writes that TabItem's value, otherwise the selection is view state that is not saved

geo.note: every panel is measured, so switching tabs never changes the height

states.text: each tab's label and text form in order

work.visits: 1 + tabs + the visits of every panel
work.note: every panel is measured and laid out for its height, so every panel's visits are charged to accounts.perRevision and its nodes to the output node limit (spec §9.4)

ex.src:
<Tabs>
<TabItem label="Summary">
All checks passed.
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Details">
No warnings.
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

TabItem.sum: One tab: a label and its content.

List.sum: ListItems in a fixed viewport of displayRows items; Each builds them; more pages through a PagedList.

data.more: the open page drives LoadMore and auto_load_more for that PagedList (spec §8.6); the footer shows its status, done or capped

geo.note: items beyond the viewport are on the open page, never in the row; a transcript row shows at most 10, a page up to 50

states.empty: the empty text in the first slot
states.error: the error in the first slot; footer shows the code
states.text: the first displayRows items' titles, one per line

List.openPage: an app-owned scrolling page of every item, with its own end sentinel for auto_load_more

ListItem.sum: One List row: a title, an optional subtitle and trailing text.

geo.note: the subtitle line is reserved whether or not it is given; each line is cut, never wrapped; tone draws a leading dot

LiveOutput.sum: The last lines of a Watch, in a fixed box with its live, ended or error status.

source.shape: watch items; each item is a string, or a record whose field member is a string; anything else draws …

geo.note: lines are cut, never wrapped; new lines replace old ones inside the box

states.ready: footer 'Live', 'Ended' or the error, and '{dropped} earlier lines not shown' when dropped > 0

ex.src:
export const live = Watch("bash_watch", {})

<LiveOutput source={live} displayRows={12} />

Stat.sum: One labelled figure, with an optional caption.

geo.note: each line is cut, never wrapped; a number value shows in canonical form, so format it with FormatNumber first

ex.src:
export const total = 1250

<Stat label="Total" value={FormatNumber(total)} caption="All regions" />

Progress.sum: A bar from 0 to 100 with an optional label; an absent value draws an empty bar.

host.note: Drawn by the app, never written as tags. Their geometry is pinned here because rows that contain them are measured like any other.

ReferenceChip.sum: $$tc(N) in Markdown text: a chip that opens the snapshot.

geo.note: label is 'output of {tool}', the tool name cut at clip.chip scalars; before the reply is stored it is 'tool output' (spec §3.10)

ErrorCell.sum: A component whose height-deciding prop is an error or missing (states.propError).

geo.note: first line 'Couldn't show {Component}', second line the code

TaskCheckbox.sum: A GFM task list box, read-only (spec §3.4).

LoadingRoot.sum: The program's root during the first-answer wait (spec §8.3).

geo.note: the show_ui title on one line, then 'Loading…'; on a page the first real tree commits as a new measured revision; in a transcript row it draws inside the RowFrame

RowFrame.sum: The fixed frame of a show_ui row in the transcript, with its app-owned Open bar (geometry.rowFrame).

geo.note: later revisions draw top-aligned inside it and clip; the Open bar reads 'Open to see all' when the current revision is taller than the frame

ProgramFallback.sum: A program that failed its check or aborted (spec §9.6, §11.1).

geo.h: 2*k.cardPad + T(fallback, body, W - 2*k.cardPad, inf) + k.gap.m + k.tap
geo.note: the stored fallback text (at most 4,096 scalars) and the app-owned Reset button

GenericToolRow.sum: Today's tool row, used when a tool view is missing, older, unapproved or failed (spec §11.2).

ArgumentsShortened.sum: The host's label on a row whose input projection was cut (spec §2.3).

ReplyShortened.sum: The marker after the first 256 KiB of a reply (spec §3.1).

Markdown.sum: Paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, code fences and GFM tables (spec §3.4).

geo.h: the prose measurer's height at W (AgentTurnBodyView rules), with inline components as fixed-size attachments
geo.note: network decides whether links are styled as links or as text; it does not change metrics

replyReduced.note: Table only with written data; derived by teaching.reply.filter, listed here so a test can compare

replyTaught.needs: refs and handles, no maps (every v1 runner)
replyTaught.note: Map is valid in replies but taught to nobody until a provider produces map records

profilesAllow.rule: derived from each component's in; listed for review and tests. tool_row holds no control, site, media, table or code block: a row shows counts and codes and opens its page on a tap. tool_row and tool_page hold no Citation, Image, ImageGroup or Map: templates have no references, and no operation returns scoped media in v1.

open.item: the terminal app's layout table in cells
a computer-side maker of Map records (static raster and place positions) at store time, and the maps capability that advertises it
open.owner: a provider not yet named; depends on the output_refs contract (design-note open question 3)

open.item: the language crate's machine-readable export of its function table and profile rules, generated from the crate, for show_ui teaching
open.owner: occipital; shape left to the crate

open.item: whether tool_row revisions (running to finished) should keep their insertion height like show_ui rows

deferred: FollowUpBlock (Compose in a Button covers it)
pie, area, radar and scatter charts

admission.minor: A new component, a new optional prop or a new enum value is a minor catalog version (1.1). It ships in apps before any teaching names it; an app that predates it shows the tag as text, and its reports are suppressed (spec §12.3).
admission.major: Removing or renaming anything, changing a default, a range, a geometry formula's meaning or a state's look that changes height is a major version, or for geometry alone a new layoutVersion.
admission.layoutVersion: Changing a constant in layouts or a formula without changing what is valid bumps layoutVersion; every cached height is keyed by it.
required: a complete entry: sum, in, flow, kids, props with types/defaults/ranges, data shapes, geo with hIn, every state, text form and work
renderer conformance fixtures: measured equals drawn for every state at the fixture widths and text sizes, on every app
a device benchmark of background measurement and decode on the oldest supported phone
an effect review for any action prop: which steps it may carry; v1 admits no write
a media review for any prop that loads pixels: handle or snapshot only, decode caps, no nested resources
teaching examples that compile against the exact dialect, catalog digest and registry
admission.replay: Replies and programs store the catalog digest they were checked against; an app draws them with that catalog or shows their text form, never with a newer one (spec §13.2).
